strengths.title: Proficient Python programming
strengths.why_it_matters: The role requires writing robust Python services for model serving and data processing.
strengths.evidence_quote: Wrote Python scripts to clean customer data and train churn prediction models.

strengths.title: Solid machine‑learning fundamentals
strengths.why_it_matters: You’ll need to evaluate model outputs and track quality metrics for RAG pipelines.
strengths.evidence_quote: Trained a scikit-learn random forest and a small PyTorch CNN on 5,000 leaf images.

strengths.title: Hands‑on experience with LLMs and Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
strengths.why_it_matters: Building and improving RAG pipelines over customer documents is a core responsibility.
strengths.evidence_quote: Built a retrieval-augmented chatbot over 300 university policy PDFs using LangChain and FAISS.

strengths.title: FastAPI REST‑API development
strengths.why_it_matters: The job expects you to expose models through streaming FastAPI endpoints.
strengths.evidence_quote: Served the assistant through a FastAPI REST API with streaming responses.

strengths.title: Effective Git collaboration
strengths.why_it_matters: Team work is done via pull requests and code reviews on GitHub.
strengths.evidence_quote: Collaborated through pull requests and code review on GitHub.

questions: Can you walk me through the architecture of the Campus Policy Assistant you built, focusing on how you indexed the PDFs and retrieved relevant passages?
How did you measure answer faithfulness, and what steps did you take to reduce hallucinations by 40%?
What trade‑offs did you consider when choosing FAISS versus other vector stores?
Explain how you implemented streaming responses in FastAPI for the chatbot.
Which HTTP status codes do you return for successful queries, client errors, and server errors, and why?
Describe the difference between precision and recall and give an example of when you would prioritize one over the other in evaluating a RAG system.
What is overfitting, and how did you guard against it in your Crop Disease Classifier project?
Tell me about a time you faced a merge conflict during a pull request. How did you resolve it?
Walk me through how you contribute a new feature to a shared repository using Git and GitHub.
The role may involve storing document metadata in a relational database. How would you design a simple schema for PDFs and their vector IDs?
Write a SQL query that joins a `documents` table with a `vectors` table to fetch the top‑k most similar vectors for a given document ID.
Tell me about a time you worked in a team and faced a disagreement. How did you handle it and what was the outcome?
Give an example of how you used feedback from a code review to improve your implementation.

tasks: Read the PostgreSQL tutorial and take notes on CREATE TABLE, primary/foreign keys, and basic SELECT syntax.
Design a simple schema for storing PDF metadata and vector IDs; write the CREATE statements.
Practice writing JOIN queries that retrieve document text together with its vector representation.
Review the FAISS documentation and the Supabase AI vectors guide to understand indexing parameters.
Add a second vector store (e.g., Supabase) to the Campus Policy Assistant project and compare retrieval latency.
Write a short blog‑style summary of the differences between FAISS and other vector DBs.
Create a Dockerfile for the FastAPI service that installs dependencies and runs the app.
Build and run the container locally, verifying that the API endpoint works.
Write a brief README explaining how to spin up the service with Docker.
Watch a short introductory video on deploying FastAPI on AWS Elastic Beanstalk or GCP Cloud Run (use free YouTube resources).
Sketch a deployment diagram showing where the vector store, API, and monitoring would live in the cloud.
List three cloud services you would consider for scaling the RAG pipeline.
Review evaluation techniques for RAG (faithfulness, relevance, latency).
Create a one‑page cheat sheet with formulas and thresholds you used in the Campus Policy Assistant.
Run a quick re‑evaluation on a new set of 20 questions to practice metric calculation.
Read the FastAPI tutorial sections on dependency injection and background tasks.
Add input validation with Pydantic models to your API endpoints.
Implement proper error handling and map exceptions to appropriate HTTP status codes.
Do a timed mock interview covering the question groups above; record your answers.
Review the recording, note any hesitations or gaps, and refine your STAR stories.
Ask a peer or mentor to give feedback on technical depth and communication clarity.
